intro: The analysis for the SSC CGL 2026 Tier 1 exam held on 23 October 2026 compiles candidate feedback from three shifts. Shifts 1 and 2 have full reports, while shift 3 has a partial review that requires further corroboration. Unofficial figures suggest that candidates in shifts 1 and 2 attempted between 65 and 82 questions overall, with attempts ranging 17–24 per section; SSC normally normalises scores across shifts. Reasoning was generally perceived as easy to moderate, quantitative aptitude as the most challenging, and English as relatively easy. All numbers are unofficial and should be interpreted accordingly.

faqs.q: What was the overall difficulty level reported for the SSC CGL 2026 Tier 1 exam on 23 October 2026?
faqs.a: Shifts 1 and 2 were reported as moderate overall, while shift 3 was described as easy. The shift 3 assessment is partial and awaits further confirmation.

faqs.q: How did candidates describe the Quantitative Aptitude section on 23 October 2026?
faqs.a: In shifts 1 and 2, Quantitative Aptitude was widely seen as difficult, with time pressure limiting attempts. In shift 3, the section was reported as easy, but the review is partial and needs corroboration.

faqs.q: What are the unofficial good attempt ranges for the shifts on 23 October 2026?
faqs.a: Shift 1 reported a good attempt range of 65–82 questions overall, and shift 2 reported 65–77. For shift 3, good attempt numbers were not reliably reported, so no figure is provided.

faqs.q: Is there a complete analysis available for shift 3 of the 23 October 2026 exam?
faqs.a: Only a limited (partial) review for shift 3 has been published. It offers an initial impression of the paper but requires additional evidence before a full analysis can be considered reliable.

faqs.q: How does SSC handle scoring across different shifts for the 23 October 2026 exam?
faqs.a: SSC normalises scores across shifts to ensure comparability, meaning that raw marks from each shift are adjusted according to a standardisation process before final ranking.
